Offline calculation dashboard

Fixed versus freely varying capacity

Both alternatives retain the same demand, free-flow speed, fitted duration, delay and discharge. Each finds its best emission-target queue speed within the same jam-density and wave-speed bounds. The free-capacity column allows the implied capacity to change.

The earlier bounded analysis already allowed a capacity change when needed to reach its optimal speed. Its preference for preserving capacity was a secondary choice among equally good emission solutions. The free-capacity results here reproduce that optimum; the new comparison is against a strictly fixed capacity.

Strictly fixed capacity

kj=C0vf+C0ω
vq=μ0C0vf+C0−μ0ω

Capacity may vary

kj(ω)=μ0q+μ0ω
C*=vfω*kj*vf+ω*

Capacity is calculated from each candidate pair, with no requirement that it equal the current capacity.

Emission targets and physical limit
minimizeq|MCO₂(q)OCO₂−1|
J(q)=14∑p(Mp(q)Op−1)2
Normalized RMSE (%)=100J
0<q≤LTf+wpeak^

Primary bounds: 150–300 veh/mi/lane for jam density and 5–20 mph for the backward-wave magnitude. The expanded bounds lower the latter to 3 mph. Primary fixed capacity is feasible for 136/137 episodes; free capacity is feasible for all 137. Compare pooled errors on the same feasible cases. These are conditional fits to O, the recorded-speed emission reference, not independently validated capacities.
